questions.question: What is the core authorization invariant for a red-team action?
options: It must stay inside a documented authorization, operating envelope, stop condition, and recovery plan
It is permitted whenever the operator believes it will improve coverage
It is permitted when the target is owned by the same company
It is permitted after an alert has fired
questions.explanation: Ownership alone is not authorization. The exact target, behavior, time, safeguards, and recovery path must be approved before execution.

questions.question: How should MITRE ATT&CK be used in an engagement plan?
options: As a shared vocabulary for threat-informed behavior and defensive evidence
As a checklist requiring every technique to be executed
As proof that a selected behavior is safe
As a replacement for rules of engagement
questions.explanation: ATT&CK adds a consistent behavioral vocabulary, but authorization, safety, environment knowledge, and evidence design remain separate responsibilities.

questions.question: A planned action reaches an excluded third-party tenant. What is the correct decision?
options: Stop and contact the white cell
Continue if no sensitive data is opened
Continue but omit the tenant from the report
Ask the operator to lower the activity rate
questions.explanation: Crossing an explicit exclusion is a scope violation. The exercise must fail closed and escalate through the named control channel.

questions.question: An alert exists, but there is no execution ID or matching source telemetry. What can the team conclude?
options: The evidence chain is incomplete
The defensive control is validated
The red-team action was blocked
The finding can be closed
questions.explanation: A timestamp-adjacent alert does not prove causality. Execution and control records must be linked before making a control claim.

questions.question: A remediation is deployed with a change ticket. What is still required before verified closure?
options: A passed retest against the same bounded hypothesis
A higher severity score
A second operator
A longer engagement window
questions.explanation: Deployment proves that a change shipped, not that it corrected the observed defensive gap.

questions.question: Which metric most directly supports program improvement?
options: Open finding age and failed retests by control version
Volume of data the operators accessed
Number of days the team stayed undetected
Total number of ATT&CK techniques attempted
questions.explanation: Owned remediation and retest evidence describe whether control gaps are actually being corrected. Activity volume can reward unnecessary risk.

questions.question: When should a red-team exercise stop even if the original test hypothesis is being answered?
options: When an approved stop condition or real incident occurs
Only when every planned action is complete
Only after the final report is drafted
When the blue team detects the exercise
questions.explanation: Safety and real incident response take precedence. Detection alone may be an expected observation unless the rules of engagement define it as a stop condition.
